title: We made 32 free, offline asset tools for coding agents: pivots, colliders, palette swaps, loop checks (open source)
author: ludoaiplatform
selftext:
This one doesn't need a Ludo account: our CLI now has a **free** toolbox for the boring asset work your coding agent otherwise guesses at. It works on the assets **you already have**: any spritesheet, image, sound or glTF model, not just ours.

What's in it:

\- **Engine setup**: pivot on the character's feet, a box and capsule collider that leaves the sword out, and one pixels-per-unit across all of a character's sheets. It writes Godot SpriteFrames, Unity .meta + .anim, and a TexturePacker atlas for Phaser and PixiJS.  
\- **Spritesheets**: slice, join, put a character's moves in one frame size with the feet on one ground line, score how cleanly a loop closes, export a GIF or WebM.  
\- **Pixel art**: recolor to any Lospec palette, swap colours, add an outline or a drop shadow. On a sheet, every frame gets the same edit.  
\- **Textures**: checks whether a tile is seamless before it's in your level, and writes Tiled, Godot and Unity tilesets.  
\- **Audio and 3D**: loudness, true peak, loop clicks and BPM; for a GLB, triangles, rig, which way it faces, and how fast to move it so the walk's feet don't slide.  
\- **Asset folder check**: lists what's in your assets folder and what's missing next to the rest (two characters have a jump, the third doesn't).

Every tool returns plain JSON, so the agent works from numbers instead of eyeballing the image, and `--overlay` saves a picture so it can check its own collider. In the video, Claude Code does the knight's setup from one sentence.

    npm install -g /cli
    ludo skill install

The second line is for Claude Code; Codex, Cursor and Copilot get it with `npx skills add Ludo-AI/ludo-cli`. Runs on your machine, no account, no credits, MIT. The CLI sends a short usage record of each command (its name and the flag names, never their values, paths or file contents); `LUDO_TELEMETRY=0` turns it off. When the folder check finds a gap, it suggests the Ludo command that makes it, and that part does need an account. Every tool above works without one.

Repo: [https://github.com/Ludo-AI/ludo-cli](https://github.com/Ludo-AI/ludo-cli)  
All the tools with real runs: [https://ludo.ai/developers/toolbox](https://ludo.ai/developers/toolbox)

What asset chores do you still do by hand between the generator and the engine? I'd like to know which ones are missing.
